drafts.introduction_replacement: Case-level quality estimation without a new manual mask has been studied with reverse classification accuracy [3]. For promptable models, Kinalioglu fused structural responses to prompt perturbations with confidence and reported failure recovery after rejecting the highest-risk tenth of masks [4]. Loke et al. compared prompt-perturbation uncertainty with predicted IoU, entropy and test-time augmentation across SAM/MedSAM settings using paired tests and multiplicity control [5]. These studies establish relevant scoring and ranking comparisons. Here, the contribution is an operating-policy evaluation in breast ultrasound: development-calibrated numerical cutoffs are transferred unchanged to internal and external patients, then interpreted alongside rankings at the same actual review count. Joint reporting of detection, review fraction and misses distinguishes transfer of a cutoff from allocation of a specified review capacity.
drafts.discussion_paragraph: Prior work already includes budget-constrained failure screening: Kinalioglu reported failure recovery in the highest-risk 10% [4], while Loke et al. evaluated case-level discrimination and error correlation across datasets and prompt regimes [5]. Our analysis links a development review target to the numerical cutoff deployed on another dataset and compares that operating point with the same-count ranking curves. The transferred cutoff leaves workload as an outcome; the ranking rule fixes how many patients are selected. The additional development-, test- and combined-resampling routes describe uncertainty in calibration and test sampling for this operating example. This scope supports a policy- and budget-specific interpretation of the observed detections.

safe_increment: The specific breast-ultrasound workflow coupling a development-calibrated review-score cutoff, unchanged cross-dataset transfer, joint detection/workload/miss reporting, and same-actual-count rankings, with calibration/test resampling separated.
required_acknowledgment: Reference4 already reports failure recovery at a fixed rejection fraction. Reference5 already directly compares perturbation uncertainty with model confidence across models/datasets and includes synthetic non-oracle prompt checks.
